proof_summary: Successive binomial ratios are written as products \(U_x=\prod_{p\nmid k}(1+xp^r/k)\); pairing \(k\) with \(p^r-k\) and using vanishing reciprocal sums gives \(U_2^2-1=3(U_1^2-1)=6(U_1-1)\), while congruences for the preceding binomial coefficients supply the complementary \(p\)-adic divisibility needed for the final cancellation. The case \(r=2\) uses a finer truncated product expansion for \(p\ge7\), with the remaining cases \(p=3,5\) settled by direct finite computation.
